added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run baseline_suite and after_suite logs: both complete, EXIT=0, no FAILED ids; summaries 58 passed and 62 passed. The red base and mutation logs provide positive controls for failure-id extraction.
assertion_independence: No added assertion compares an output to itself or to an expectation obtained from that same output; snapshots are captured before mutation, committed blobs are queried independently, and literal identity/narrative expectations specify the operation contract.

assertion_review.fails_when: The store hook is reached for the wrong project/run, before the landing comment differs from HEAD, or before the per-run file is written; these assertions prove the refusal is injected after the forward writes.
Promotion swallows the append refusal or changes its refusal type/message; restoring the base ordering leaves this expectation green, so it is a refusal-shape check rather than the restoration guard.
Removing the new rollback leaves the post-call plan bytes different from the bytes captured before promotion; the fixture committed those bytes before the capture, independently of rollback.
A staged or unstaged change remains at the plan path after refusal, including an index-only residue that the byte comparison alone cannot detect.
A refused promotion changes repository HEAD; the independent reference was read with git before invoking promotion.
A refused promotion deletes or rewrites the live pointer; the independent bytes were captured before promotion.
The refused append leaves its newly written run projection on disk; this pins existing ledger cleanup alongside the plan repair.
The store refusal stops being raised; this is a refusal-shape check and does not alone establish rollback.
Restoring base promotion code leaves the plan dirty, making the real require_plan_section_visible call raise PlanVisibilityError instead of returning the pre-call revision.
A successful promotion stops reporting a recorded plan comment; this is a success-path flag check, backed independently by the committed payload assertion.
Successful promotion omits its narrative from the committed HEAD plan; the literal expected narrative is required output and is independently read from git.
Successful promotion leaves the working plan content different from the committed HEAD blob.
Successful promotion leaves a staged or unstaged plan change.
Successful promotion leaves the plan dirty or dispatch returns a revision different from independently read git HEAD; this validates the runtime visibility reader against the repository.
Successful promotion leaves no readable run row, the wrong run row or an unexpected duplicate in the isolated fixture ledger.
